expected_assertion: Two canonical fact rows written: (vendor_id='quickbooks_time', vendor_entity_id='901001') and (vendor_id='seven_shifts', vendor_entity_id='901001'). Adapter idempotency UNIQUE is `(vendor_id, operator_id, vendor_entity_id, vendor_modified_at)` — vendor_id partitions the namespace so a colliding integer id from a different labor vendor does not overwrite the QBT row.
notes: QuickBooks Time `timesheets[].id` is a small monotonic integer (per vendor doc). Other labor vendors (7shifts, ADP, Humanity, Push Operations, Agendrix) use the same numeric-id shape, so collisions are inevitable in any operator running two labor vendors during a migration window. The framework's idempotency namespace prefixes by `vendor_id`, which is the primary defense.
